# Send a daily Asana project digest to Discord

**Pattern:** Schedule -> read -> summarise -> notify · **Level:** Production · **Trigger:** Schedule (daily)

## What it does
Reads the incomplete tasks in an Asana project each morning and posts a grouped, counted digest to Discord — an async standup ready before anyone logs on.

## Why it exists
Live standups are expensive and board-checking is tedious. A daily digest gives the whole team the state of the project in one message, grouped by owner, with overdue and due-today work surfaced.

## Main flow
Every Morning 08:30 -> Get Incomplete Tasks -> Build Digest by Assignee -> Format Message -> Post Digest to Discord (failure -> error rail).

## Use it for
- A distributed team dropping the live standup
- A morning 'state of the project' post
- Daily client-channel updates with no manual work

## You get
- A standup that writes itself
- Grouped by assignee; overdue/due-today up top
- One scheduled message vs everyone checking Asana

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Asana access token; Discord webhook URL.
Colour key: 🟦 entry · 🟫 app I/O · ⬜ logic · 🟩 output · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
This runs on a timer; the Asana read is pinned so you can preview the digest before connecting anything. Sample data is pinned on the trigger, so hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow end to end before attaching a single credential. Right-click → Unpin when you go live.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never bundled in a template. Every node that talks to an external service needs its own connection before the first real run — open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Asana access token**
Asana → My Settings → Apps → Manage Developer Apps → Create Personal Access Token. Paste it into n8n's Asana credential.
_Gotcha:_ The token inherits your Asana permissions — it can only read/write projects your own account can see.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy Webhook URL. Paste it into n8n's Discord Webhook credential.
_Gotcha:_ A webhook URL is bound to one channel. Use a separate webhook/credential per channel you post to.

Set each credential up once; it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Nothing happens when the event should fire**
Cause: The workflow is still a draft, or its trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate it. The manual test URL is different from the production URL.

**A node shows a red triangle right after import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials note).

**The digest is empty**
Cause: completed_since=now returned nothing, or the project GID is wrong.
Fix: completed_since=now returns only incomplete tasks — an empty digest means no open work, or the wrong project GID.

**The message is cut off in Discord**
Cause: Discord hard-caps a message at 2000 characters.
Fix: Split large projects into multiple posts, or send only overdue + due-today (see Practice).

**Provider returns 429**
Cause: You are hitting the API rate limit.
Fix: The node already retries with backoff; widen the schedule interval or lower the batch size to stay under quota.

Still stuck? The **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there.

## Design decisions

The Asana read uses completed_since=now, which is Asana's idiom for 'only incomplete tasks' — filtering server-side is cheaper than pulling everything and dropping the done ones. Grouping by assignee (in one Code node) turns a flat task list into an accountable standup: everyone can find their own line. Conditional overdue/due-today lines keep a healthy project's digest clean instead of showing empty headers.

## Practice exercises

Already production-shaped — deepen it:

1. Add a section for tasks with no assignee so nothing falls through the cracks.
2. Post only when there is overdue work, to make the message signal-only.
3. Split projects over 2000 chars into a thread of messages.
